newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin pledges to pay back wages in December.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin pledges to pay back wages in December.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, addressing the upper house of parliament on Tuesday, pledged to pay wage arrears and pensions in December, but warned that regions would get less money.

"In all main spheres, except the army, 100 percent of debts will be repaid in December. This way we will make our debts disappear, and will not allow new indebtedness to form and grow," Chernomyrdin told parliament members.
"We have to fulfil our promises on pensions. We have to return to a normal regime of pension payments by the beginning of the new year," Chernomyrdin told reporters after the meeting.
He clarified that a "normal regime" meant regular payments of 12.5 trillion roubles ($2.26 billion) a month.
He said all back wages to be paid in December amounted to 7.9 trillion roubles, but he did not say where the money would come from.
Many Russian have not been paid for more than six months.

But Chernomyrdin told Russian regional administration heads, who sit in the Federation Council, that budget subsidies to the regions would be only 63.3 percent of planned levels this year due to regions' debts.
He said the government had paid 10 trillion roubles in subsidies to the regions, while they owed seven trillion roubles to the budget.
Chernomyrdin angered the upper house last week by ignoring a plea to address it, but held out an olive branch on Monday, saying he would meet the parliamentarians.
The Federation Council demanded that the government explain its failure to pay months of back wages owed to workers in the public sector.

The Council has traditionally been compliant to the demands of President Boris Yeltsin and his government, but Chernomyrdin's failure to show up last Wednesday provoked the wrath of some members of the chamber.
The government's failure to pay wages and pensions has sparked a coalminers' strike and prompted sporadic protests in various parts of the country.
Chernomyrdin said the government would pay a total of 10 trillion roubles to the ailing mining sector, instead of 7.6 trillion initially budgeted for 1996.
He said a special government commission, headed by First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin, had started tackling the crisis in Russia's main coal producing region Kuzbass. ($1=5525 Rouble)
